index 00000000..36ca0313
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/test/smtp-sink.py
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Minimal loopback SMTP sink for isolated E2E tests; discards message bodies."""
+
+import socketserver
+
+
+class Handler(socketserver.StreamRequestHandler):
+    def handle(self):
+        self.wfile.write(b"220 secman-e2e-sink\r\n")
+        in_data = False
+        for raw in self.rfile:
+            line = raw.rstrip(b"\r\n")
+            if in_data:
+                if line == b".":
+                    in_data = False
+                    self.wfile.write(b"250 accepted\r\n")
+                continue
+            command = line.split(b" ", 1)[0].upper()
+            if command in (b"EHLO", b"HELO"):
+                self.wfile.write(b"250 secman-e2e-sink\r\n")
+            elif command in (b"MAIL", b"RCPT", b"RSET", b"NOOP"):
+                self.wfile.write(b"250 ok\r\n")
+            elif command == b"DATA":
+                in_data = True
+                self.wfile.write(b"354 end with .\r\n")
+            elif command == b"QUIT":
+                self.wfile.write(b"221 bye\r\n")
+                return
+            else:
+                self.wfile.write(b"502 unsupported\r\n")
+
+
+class Server(socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer):
+    allow_reuse_address = True
+    daemon_threads = True
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    with Server(("127.0.0.1", 1925), Handler) as server:
+        server.serve_forever()

@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+package com.secman.service
+
+import com.secman.domain.Asset
+import jakarta.inject.Singleton
+import jakarta.persistence.EntityManager
+
+/** Executes one bounded inventory query without initializing asset collections. */
+@Singleton
+open class AssetOverviewQueryService(private val entityManager: EntityManager) {
+    /** Optional filters accepted by the overview endpoint. */
+    data class Filters(
+        val name: String?,
+        val ipAddress: String?,
+        val owner: String?,
+        val adDomain: String?,
+        val accountId: String?,
+        val workgroupId: Long?
+    )
+
+    /** A page of assets plus the exact matching row count. */
+    data class Result(val assets: List<Asset>, val total: Long)
+
+    /** Applies access IDs before database pagination; null IDs mean a globally authorized caller. */
+    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+    open fun search(ids: Set<Long>?, filters: Filters, page: Int, pageSize: Int): Result {
+        if (ids != null && ids.isEmpty()) return Result(emptyList(), 0)
+
+        val rows = entityManager.createNativeQuery(ROW_QUERY, Asset::class.java)
+        val count = entityManager.createNativeQuery(COUNT_QUERY)
+        bind(rows, ids, filters)
+        bind(count, ids, filters)
+        rows.firstResult = page * pageSize
+        rows.maxResults = pageSize
+        return Result(rows.resultList as List<Asset>, (count.singleResult as Number).toLong())
+    }
+
+    private fun bind(query: jakarta.persistence.Query, ids: Set<Long>?, filters: Filters) {
+        query.setParameter("restrictIds", ids != null)
+        query.setParameter("ids", ids ?: setOf(-1L))
+        query.setParameter("name", filters.name)
+        query.setParameter("ip", filters.ipAddress)
+        query.setParameter("owner", filters.owner)
+        query.setParameter("adDomain", filters.adDomain)
+        query.setParameter("accountId", filters.accountId)
+        query.setParameter("workgroupId", filters.workgroupId)
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        private const val ROW_QUERY = """
+            SELECT a.* FROM asset a
+            WHERE (:restrictIds = FALSE OR a.id IN (:ids))
+              AND (:name IS NULL OR LOCATE(LOWER(:name), LOWER(a.name)) > 0)
+              AND (:ip IS NULL OR LOCATE(LOWER(:ip), LOWER(a.ip)) > 0)
+              AND (:owner IS NULL OR LOCATE(LOWER(:owner), LOWER(a.owner)) > 0)
+              AND (:adDomain IS NULL OR LOCATE(LOWER(:adDomain), LOWER(a.ad_domain)) > 0)
+              AND (:accountId IS NULL OR LOCATE(:accountId, a.cloud_account_id) > 0)
+              AND (:workgroupId IS NULL OR EXISTS (
+                  SELECT 1 FROM asset_workgroups aw
+                  JOIN workgroup w ON w.id = aw.workgroup_id
+                  WHERE aw.asset_id = a.id AND aw.workgroup_id = :workgroupId AND w.enabled = TRUE
+              ))
+            ORDER BY a.created_at DESC, a.id DESC
+        """
+        private const val COUNT_QUERY = """
+            SELECT COUNT(*) FROM asset a
+            WHERE (:restrictIds = FALSE OR a.id IN (:ids))
+              AND (:name IS NULL OR LOCATE(LOWER(:name), LOWER(a.name)) > 0)
+              AND (:ip IS NULL OR LOCATE(LOWER(:ip), LOWER(a.ip)) > 0)
+              AND (:owner IS NULL OR LOCATE(LOWER(:owner), LOWER(a.owner)) > 0)
+              AND (:adDomain IS NULL OR LOCATE(LOWER(:adDomain), LOWER(a.ad_domain)) > 0)
+              AND (:accountId IS NULL OR LOCATE(:accountId, a.cloud_account_id) > 0)
+              AND (:workgroupId IS NULL OR EXISTS (
+                  SELECT 1 FROM asset_workgroups aw
+                  JOIN workgroup w ON w.id = aw.workgroup_id
+                  WHERE aw.asset_id = a.id AND aw.workgroup_id = :workgroupId AND w.enabled = TRUE
+              ))
+        """
+    }
+}

+import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+
+export function requireIsolatedTarget(): void {
+  const db = process.env.SECMAN_TEST_ISOLATED_DB ?? '';
+  const token = process.env.SECMAN_TEST_OWNER_TOKEN ?? '';
+  const backend = process.env.SECMAN_E2E_BACKEND_URL ?? '';
+  if (!/^secman_e2e_[a-f0-9]{16}$/.test(db) ||
+      !/^[a-f0-9]{32}$/.test(token) ||
+      process.env.DB_NAME !== db ||
+      process.env.DB_CONNECT !== `jdbc:mariadb://127.0.0.1:3306/${db}` ||
+      backend !== 'http://127.0.0.1:18080' ||
+      !process.env.DB_USER || !process.env.DB_PASS) {
+    throw new Error('Database-mutating Playwright specs require scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh');
+  }
+
+  const actualToken = execFileSync('mariadb', [
+    '--batch', '--skip-column-names', '-h', '127.0.0.1', '-u', process.env.DB_USER,
+    db, '-e', 'SELECT owner_token FROM secman_e2e_owner LIMIT 1',
+  ], {
+    encoding: 'utf8',
+    env: { ...process.env, MYSQL_PWD: process.env.DB_PASS },
+    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'],
+  }).trim();
+  if (actualToken !== token) {
+    throw new Error('Disposable database ownership marker does not match');
+  }
+}

    17	/**
    18	 * Origin validation filter for MCP Streamable HTTP Transport.
    19	 *
    20	 * Per MCP specification, servers MUST validate the Origin header when present
    21	 * to prevent CSRF attacks from malicious websites.
    22	 *
    23	 * - Requests without Origin header are allowed (non-browser clients like Claude Desktop)
    24	 * - Requests with Origin header are validated against allowed origins list
    25	 * - Localhost origins are always allowed for development
    26	 *
    27	 * @see https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2024-11-05/basic/transports
    28	 */
    29	@Filter("/mcp/**")
    30	class McpOriginValidationFilter : HttpServerFilter {
    31	
    32	    private val logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(McpOriginValidationFilter::class.java)
    33	
    34	    @Value("\${secman.mcp.transport.allowed-origins:}")
    35	    private var allowedOrigins: List<String> = emptyList()
    36	
    37	    @Value("\${secman.mcp.transport.validate-origin:true}")
    38	    private var validateOrigin: Boolean = true
    39	
    40	    companion object {
    41	        // Localhost patterns that are always allowed for development
    42	        private val LOCALHOST_PATTERNS = listOf(
    43	            Regex("^https?://localhost(:\\d+)?$"),
    44	            Regex("^https?://127\\.0\\.0\\.1(:\\d+)?$"),
    45	            Regex("^https?://\\[::1\\](:\\d+)?$")
    46	        )
    47	    }
    48	
    49	    override fun doFilter(request: HttpRequest<*>, chain: ServerFilterChain): Publisher<MutableHttpResponse<*>> {
    50	        val origin = request.headers.get("Origin")
    51	
    52	        // No Origin header - allow (non-browser clients)
    53	        if (origin == null) {
    54	            logger.debug("MCP request without Origin header - allowed (non-browser client)")
    55	            return chain.proceed(request)
    56	        }
    57	
    58	        // Origin validation disabled - allow all
    59	        if (!validateOrigin) {
    60	            logger.debug("MCP origin validation disabled - allowing: {}", origin)
    61	            return chain.proceed(request)
    62	        }
    63	
    64	        // Check if origin is allowed
    65	        if (isOriginAllowed(origin)) {
    66	            logger.debug("MCP request from allowed origin: {}", origin)
    67	            return chain.proceed(request)
    68	        }
    69	
    70	        // Origin not allowed - reject request
    71	        logger.warn("MCP request from disallowed origin rejected: {}", origin)
    72	        return Mono.just(
    73	            HttpResponse.status<Map<String, Any>>(HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN)
    74	                .body(mapOf(
    75	                    "jsonrpc" to "2.0",
    76	                    "id" to null,
    77	                    "error" to mapOf(
    78	                        "code" to -32003,
    79	                        "message" to "Origin not allowed: $origin"
    80	                    )
    81	                ))
    82	        )
    83	    }

    98	        }

    17	/**
    18	 * Origin validation filter for MCP Streamable HTTP Transport.
    19	 *
    20	 * Per MCP specification, servers MUST validate the Origin header when present
    21	 * to prevent CSRF attacks from malicious websites.
    22	 *
    23	 * - Requests without Origin header are allowed (non-browser clients like Claude Desktop)
    24	 * - Requests with Origin header are validated against allowed origins list
    25	 * - Localhost origins are always allowed for development
    26	 *
    27	 * @see https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2024-11-05/basic/transports
    28	 */
    29	@Filter("/mcp/**")
    30	class McpOriginValidationFilter : HttpServerFilter {
    31	
    32	    private val logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(McpOriginValidationFilter::class.java)
    33	
    34	    @Value("\${secman.mcp.transport.allowed-origins:}")
    35	    private var allowedOrigins: List<String> = emptyList()
    36	
    37	    @Value("\${secman.mcp.transport.validate-origin:true}")
    38	    private var validateOrigin: Boolean = true
    39	
    40	    companion object {
    41	        // Localhost patterns that are always allowed for development
    42	        private val LOCALHOST_PATTERNS = listOf(
    43	            Regex("^https?://localhost(:\\d+)?$"),
    44	            Regex("^https?://127\\.0\\.0\\.1(:\\d+)?$"),
    45	            Regex("^https?://\\[::1\\](:\\d+)?$")
    46	        )
    47	    }
    48	
    49	    override fun doFilter(request: HttpRequest<*>, chain: ServerFilterChain): Publisher<MutableHttpResponse<*>> {
    50	        val origin = request.headers.get("Origin")
    51	
    52	        // No Origin header - allow (non-browser clients)
    53	        if (origin == null) {
    54	            logger.debug("MCP request without Origin header - allowed (non-browser client)")
    55	            return chain.proceed(request)
    56	        }
    57	
    58	        // Origin validation disabled - allow all
    59	        if (!validateOrigin) {
    60	            logger.debug("MCP origin validation disabled - allowing: {}", origin)
    61	            return chain.proceed(request)
    62	        }
    63	
    64	        // Check if origin is allowed
    65	        if (isOriginAllowed(origin)) {
    66	            logger.debug("MCP request from allowed origin: {}", origin)
    67	            return chain.proceed(request)
    68	        }
    69	
    70	        // Origin not allowed - reject request
    71	        logger.warn("MCP request from disallowed origin rejected: {}", origin)
    72	        return Mono.just(
    73	            HttpResponse.status<Map<String, Any>>(HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN)
    74	                .body(mapOf(
    75	                    "jsonrpc" to "2.0",
    76	                    "id" to null,
    77	                    "error" to mapOf(
    78	                        "code" to -32003,
    79	                        "message" to "Origin not allowed: $origin"
    80	                    )
    81	                ))
    82	        )
    83	    }

    85	    /**
    86	     * Check if the given origin is allowed.
    87	     */
    88	    private fun isOriginAllowed(origin: String): Boolean {
    89	        // Localhost is always allowed for development
    90	        if (LOCALHOST_PATTERNS.any { it.matches(origin) }) {
    91	            return true
    92	        }
    93	
    94	        // Check against configured allowed origins
    95	        if (allowedOrigins.isEmpty()) {
    96	            // No explicit origins configured - allow all (backwards compatible)
    97	            return true
    98	        }

# Security Policy

## Supported versions

All releases are still beta. Patches land on `dev` only.

## Reporting

- **Email**: markus@schmall.io
- **GitHub**: [private security advisory](https://github.com/schmalle/secman/security/advisories)

Include: description, repro steps, impact assessment, suggested fix (optional). Do **not** open public issues for vulnerabilities.

## Response SLO

| | Target |
|---|---|
| Acknowledgement | 48 h |
| Initial assessment | 3 d |
| Critical fix | 24 h |
| High fix | 28h d |
| Medium fix | 30 d |

## In-tree controls

- AuthN: BCrypt, JWT, OAuth2/OIDC, Passkeys/WebAuthn, optional MFA.
- AuthZ: 9-role RBAC + row-level filtering on assets (enabled direct workgroup grants, personal AWS/AD mappings, directional sharing; ownership is metadata).
- Storage: parameterized queries (no string-built SQL); sensitive config encrypted at rest (`SECMAN_ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD`/`SALT`).
- Web: HttpOnly + Secure cookies, CSP, SameSite for CSRF.
- Imports: file-size cap, MIME and header validation.
- Audit: MCP operations and notifications logged; OAuth state retried with exponential backoff to mitigate fast-SSO races.

Maintainer: Markus Schmall — markus@schmall.io.

const model = `# SecMan diff-scan threat model

## Summary

SecMan is a Micronaut/Kotlin security-management backend with an Astro/React browser client, a Kotlin CLI, MCP JSON-RPC tools, Python scanner clients, and a Go mobile relay. The backend accepts browser-cookie, bearer-token, API-key, and delegated MCP identities, persists security and asset data in MariaDB, imports scanner data, exports reports, and sends notifications. The reviewed change set also adds a bounded asset-overview query and an isolated E2E database runner.

## Assets

- User identities, password hashes, JWTs, MFA state, API keys, and delegated-user identity.
- Asset, vulnerability, workgroup, risk, requirements, integration-finding, and notification data.
- Row-level asset visibility and role boundaries, especially ADMIN/SECCHAMPION global access versus scoped users.
- Import integrity, audit history, outbound-service credentials, and test/production database separation.
- Mobile-relay snapshot confidentiality and schema compatibility.

## Trust boundaries

- Browser or external client to backend: login accepts username/password and issues only the HttpOnly auth cookie after enabled-user, password, rate-limit, and optional MFA checks (\`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/controller/AuthController.kt:135\`, \`:169\`, \`:186\`, \`:229\`).
- Authenticated caller to asset data: \`AssetFilterService\` is the shared REST/MCP row boundary; ADMIN/SECCHAMPION are global and other callers receive only current workgroup, account, domain, or sharing grants (\`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/service/AssetFilterService.kt:18\`, \`:32\`, \`:68\`, \`:154\`).
- Scanner service account to integration ingestion: the authenticated integration controller exposes subject discovery and atomic run submission, while scanner management and binding are ADMIN-only (\`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/controller/IntegrationController.kt:14\`, \`:26\`, \`:36\`, \`:41\`, \`:46\`).
- MCP client to delegated tools: origin validation precedes authentication for browser-origin requests; non-browser requests may omit Origin, and allowed origins are configuration-controlled (\`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/filter/McpOriginValidationFilter.kt:29\`, \`:49\`, \`:64\`, \`:88\`).
- SecMan backend to mobile relay: snapshot and control envelopes are versioned, and the relay/API enforces device authentication and section policies (\`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/relay/RelayDtos.kt:16\`, \`:19\`; \`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/relay/RelaySnapshotBuilder.kt:90\`; \`src/relay/internal/api/api.go:74\`).
- Test runner to MariaDB and local services: the runner generates a marked \`secman_e2e_*\` schema, validates ownership before cleanup, and uses fixed loopback ports for its isolated stack (\`scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh:21\`, \`:49\`, \`:80\`, \`:108\`, \`:133\`).

## Attacker capabilities

Realistic attackers may control ordinary authenticated input, import payloads allowed to their role, browser-origin requests, scanner result bodies, repository-hosted test arguments, or data returned by configured external scanners. They do not initially control ADMIN/SECCHAMPION credentials, trusted server configuration, pass-cli secrets, the database administrator, or the relay signing/ingest credentials. # Security Policy

## Supported versions

All releases are still beta. Patches land on `dev` only.

## Reporting

- **Email**: markus@schmall.io
- **GitHub**: [private security advisory](https://github.com/schmalle/secman/security/advisories)

Include: description, repro steps, impact assessment, suggested fix (optional). Do **not** open public issues for vulnerabilities.

## Response SLO

| | Target |
|---|---|
| Acknowledgement | 48 h |
| Initial assessment | 3 d |
| Critical fix | 24 h |
| High fix | 28h d |
| Medium fix | 30 d |

## In-tree controls

- AuthN: BCrypt, JWT, OAuth2/OIDC, Passkeys/WebAuthn, optional MFA.
- AuthZ: 9-role RBAC + row-level filtering on assets (enabled direct workgroup grants, personal AWS/AD mappings, directional sharing; ownership is metadata).
- Storage: parameterized queries (no string-built SQL); sensitive config encrypted at rest (`SECMAN_ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD`/`SALT`).
- Web: HttpOnly + Secure cookies, CSP, SameSite for CSRF.
- Imports: file-size cap, MIME and header validation.
- Audit: MCP operations and notifications logged; OAuth state retried with exponential backoff to mitigate fast-SSO races.

Maintainer: Markus Schmall — markus@schmall.io.

# SecMan diff-scan threat model

## Summary

SecMan is a Micronaut/Kotlin security-management backend with an Astro/React browser client, a Kotlin CLI, MCP JSON-RPC tools, Python scanner clients, and a Go mobile relay. The backend accepts browser-cookie, bearer-token, API-key, and delegated MCP identities, persists security and asset data in MariaDB, imports scanner data, exports reports, and sends notifications. The reviewed change set also adds a bounded asset-overview query and an isolated E2E database runner.

## Assets

- User identities, password hashes, JWTs, MFA state, API keys, and delegated-user identity.
- Asset, vulnerability, workgroup, risk, requirements, integration-finding, and notification data.
- Row-level asset visibility and role boundaries, especially ADMIN/SECCHAMPION global access versus scoped users.
- Import integrity, audit history, outbound-service credentials, and test/production database separation.
- Mobile-relay snapshot confidentiality and schema compatibility.

## Trust boundaries

- Browser or external client to backend: login accepts username/password and issues only the HttpOnly auth cookie after enabled-user, password, rate-limit, and optional MFA checks (`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/controller/AuthController.kt:135`, `:169`, `:186`, `:229`).
- Authenticated caller to asset data: `AssetFilterService` is the shared REST/MCP row boundary; ADMIN/SECCHAMPION are global and other callers receive only current workgroup, account, domain, or sharing grants (`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/service/AssetFilterService.kt:18`, `:32`, `:68`, `:154`).
- Scanner service account to integration ingestion: the authenticated integration controller exposes subject discovery and atomic run submission, while scanner management and binding are ADMIN-only (`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/controller/IntegrationController.kt:14`, `:26`, `:36`, `:41`, `:46`).
- MCP client to delegated tools: origin validation precedes authentication for browser-origin requests; non-browser requests may omit Origin, and allowed origins are configuration-controlled (`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/filter/McpOriginValidationFilter.kt:29`, `:49`, `:64`, `:88`).
- SecMan backend to mobile relay: snapshot and control envelopes are versioned, and the relay/API enforces device authentication and section policies (`src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/relay/RelayDtos.kt:16`, `:19`; `src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/relay/RelaySnapshotBuilder.kt:90`; `src/relay/internal/api/api.go:74`).
- Test runner to MariaDB and local services: the runner generates a marked `secman_e2e_*` schema, validates ownership before cleanup, and uses fixed loopback ports for its isolated stack (`scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh:21`, `:49`, `:80`, `:108`, `:133`).

## Attacker capabilities

Realistic attackers may control ordinary authenticated input, import payloads allowed to their role, browser-origin requests, scanner result bodies, repository-hosted test arguments, or data returned by configured external scanners. They do not initially control ADMIN/SECCHAMPION credentials, trusted server configuration, pass-cli secrets, the database administrator, or the relay signing/ingest credentials. Relevant capability gains would be cross-user asset access, privilege escalation, injection into SQL or shell execution, credential disclosure, production-database destruction, or unauthorized relay data.

## Security objectives

- Authenticate through established providers and never expose JWTs or secrets to JavaScript, logs, source, or response DTOs.
- Enforce `@Secured` at every endpoint and apply `AssetFilterService` before reading or mutating scoped entities.
- Bind every SQL value; constrain identifiers that cannot be bound.
- Validate file size, type, structure, and XML parser settings before import.
- Keep E2E schemas provably runner-owned and fail closed rather than touching unverified or persistent databases.
- Validate outbound destinations and redirects, preserve security headers and explicit credentialed CORS origins, and keep relay schemas/sections synchronized.
- Log security-relevant actor, target, and outcome without credential material.

## Assumptions and review focus

The formal scan covers committed changes from `117d73b5ffd9df87ed6f575a443d1a172a94d06c` through `adcc6ab8804059a2b2c9a0a248474b4b90ff7be0`. Uncommitted frontend/E2E layout changes are reviewed separately by the parent because the workbench rejected the combined working-tree target. Runtime deployment exposure, production secret values, database grants, and external-provider behavior are not established by this static scan. Scenarios are hypotheses until validated against the changed source; the required report threshold for this finalizer is HIGH or CRITICAL.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Remove one explicitly retained manual fixture recorded by create-test-data.sh.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+MANIFEST_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.e2e-logs/manual-fixtures"
+[[ $# -eq 1 ]] || { echo "Usage: $0 <fixture-manifest.json>" >&2; exit 2; }
+MANIFEST="$(realpath "$1")"
+[[ "$MANIFEST" == "$MANIFEST_DIR/"* && -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || {
+    echo "Manifest must be a recorded manual fixture under $MANIFEST_DIR" >&2; exit 2;
+}
+
+if [[ -z "${SECMAN_HOST_RESOLVED:-}" ]]; then
+    export SECMAN_HOST="pass://Test/SECMAN/SECMAN_HOST"
+    export SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME="pass://Test/SECMAN/SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME"
+    export SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS="pass://Test/SECMAN/SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS"
+    export SECMAN_USER_PASS="pass://Test/SECMAN/SECMAN_USER_PASS"
+    export SECMAN_HOST_RESOLVED=1
+    exec pass-cli run -- "$0" "$MANIFEST"
+fi
+
+for name in SECMAN_HOST SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS SECMAN_USER_PASS; do
+    [[ -n "${!name:-}" ]] || { echo "Missing $name" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+BASE_URL="$SECMAN_HOST"
+[[ "$BASE_URL" == http://* || "$BASE_URL" == https://* ]] || BASE_URL="https://$BASE_URL"
+BASE_URL="${BASE_URL%/}"
+
+target="$(jq -r '.target // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+[[ "$target" == "$BASE_URL" ]] || {
+    echo "Fixture target differs from the current SecMan host; refusing cleanup" >&2; exit 2;
+}
+
+user_name="$(jq -r '.userName // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+user_email="$(jq -r '.userEmail // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+asset_name="$(jq -r '.assetName // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+user_id="$(jq -r '.userId // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+asset_id="$(jq -r '.assetId // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+request_id="$(jq -r '.requestId // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+[[ "$user_name" == testdata-user-* && "$asset_name" == testdata-host-* ]] || {
+    echo "Manifest lacks manual fixture identity" >&2; exit 2;
+}
+
+admin_jar="$(mktemp)"
+user_jar="$(mktemp)"
+response_file="$(mktemp)"
+trap 'rm -f "$admin_jar" "$user_jar" "$response_file"' EXIT
+
+login() {
+    local jar="$1" name="$2" password="$3" status
+    status="$(curl -sS -o "$response_file" -w '%{http_code}' -c "$jar" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/auth/login" \
+        --data "$(jq -nc --arg u "$name" --arg p "$password" '{username:$u,password:$p}')")"
+    [[ "$status" == 200 ]] || { echo "Login failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; return 1; }
+}
+
+get_status() {
+    curl -sS -o "$response_file" -w '%{http_code}' -b "$1" "$BASE_URL$2"
+}
+
+delete_status() {
+    curl -sS -o "$response_file" -w '%{http_code}' -b "$1" -X DELETE "$BASE_URL$2"
+}
+
+login "$admin_jar" "$SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME" "$SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS"
+
+if [[ "$request_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    status="$(get_status "$admin_jar" "/api/vulnerability-exception-requests/$request_id")"
+    if [[ "$status" == 200 ]]; then
+        jq -e --argjson id "$request_id" --argjson user "$user_id" \
+            --argjson asset "$asset_id" --arg name "$user_name" \
+            '.id==$id and .requestedByUserId==$user and .assetId==$asset and .requestedByUsername==$name' \
+            "$response_file" >/dev/null || {
+                echo "Exception request identity mismatch; preserving it" >&2; exit 1;
+            }
+        login "$user_jar" "$user_name" "$SECMAN_USER_PASS"
+        status="$(delete_status "$user_jar" "/api/vulnerability-exception-requests/$request_id/delete")"
+        [[ "$status" == 204 ]] || { echo "Request cleanup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1; }
+    elif [[ "$status" != 404 ]]; then
+        echo "Request lookup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+
+if [[ "$asset_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    status="$(get_status "$admin_jar" "/api/assets/$asset_id")"
+    if [[ "$status" == 200 ]]; then
+        jq -e --argjson id "$asset_id" --arg name "$asset_name" \
+            '.id==$id and .name==$name' "$response_file" >/dev/null || {
+                echo "Asset identity mismatch; preserving it" >&2; exit 1;
+            }
+        status="$(delete_status "$admin_jar" "/api/assets/$asset_id")"
+        [[ "$status" == 204 || "$status" == 200 ]] || {
+            echo "Asset cleanup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1;
+        }
+    elif [[ "$status" != 404 ]]; then
+        echo "Asset lookup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+
+if [[ "$user_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    status="$(get_status "$admin_jar" "/api/users/$user_id")"
+    if [[ "$status" == 200 ]]; then
+        jq -e --argjson id "$user_id" --arg name "$user_name" --arg email "$user_email" \
+            '.id==$id and .username==$name and .email==$email' "$response_file" >/dev/null || {
+                echo "User identity mismatch; preserving it" >&2; exit 1;
+            }
+        status="$(delete_status "$admin_jar" "/api/users/$user_id")"
+        [[ "$status" == 204 || "$status" == 200 ]] || {
+            echo "User cleanup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1;
+        }
+    elif [[ "$status" != 404 ]]; then
+        echo "User lookup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+
+temp="$(mktemp "$MANIFEST.XXXXXX")"
+jq --arg cleaned "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '.cleanedAt=$cleaned' "$MANIFEST" > "$temp"
+mv "$temp" "$MANIFEST"
+echo "Manual fixture cleanup completed: $MANIFEST"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Remove one explicitly retained manual fixture recorded by create-test-data.sh.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+MANIFEST_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.e2e-logs/manual-fixtures"
+[[ $# -eq 1 ]] || { echo "Usage: $0 <fixture-manifest.json>" >&2; exit 2; }
+MANIFEST="$(realpath "$1")"
+[[ "$MANIFEST" == "$MANIFEST_DIR/"* && -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || {
+    echo "Manifest must be a recorded manual fixture under $MANIFEST_DIR" >&2; exit 2;
+}
+
+if [[ -z "${SECMAN_HOST_RESOLVED:-}" ]]; then
+    export SECMAN_HOST="pass://Test/SECMAN/SECMAN_HOST"
+    export SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME="pass://Test/SECMAN/SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME"
+    export SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS="pass://Test/SECMAN/SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS"
+    export SECMAN_USER_PASS="pass://Test/SECMAN/SECMAN_USER_PASS"
+    export SECMAN_HOST_RESOLVED=1
+    exec pass-cli run -- "$0" "$MANIFEST"
+fi
+
+for name in SECMAN_HOST SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS SECMAN_USER_PASS; do
+    [[ -n "${!name:-}" ]] || { echo "Missing $name" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+BASE_URL="$SECMAN_HOST"
+[[ "$BASE_URL" == http://* || "$BASE_URL" == https://* ]] || BASE_URL="https://$BASE_URL"
+BASE_URL="${BASE_URL%/}"
+
+target="$(jq -r '.target // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+[[ "$target" == "$BASE_URL" ]] || {
+    echo "Fixture target differs from the current SecMan host; refusing cleanup" >&2; exit 2;
+}
+
+user_name="$(jq -r '.userName // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+user_email="$(jq -r '.userEmail // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+asset_name="$(jq -r '.assetName // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+user_id="$(jq -r '.userId // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+asset_id="$(jq -r '.assetId // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+request_id="$(jq -r '.requestId // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
+[[ "$user_name" == testdata-user-* && "$asset_name" == testdata-host-* ]] || {
+    echo "Manifest lacks manual fixture identity" >&2; exit 2;
+}
+
+admin_jar="$(mktemp)"
+user_jar="$(mktemp)"
+response_file="$(mktemp)"
+trap 'rm -f "$admin_jar" "$user_jar" "$response_file"' EXIT
+
+login() {
+    local jar="$1" name="$2" password="$3" status
+    status="$(curl -sS -o "$response_file" -w '%{http_code}' -c "$jar" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/auth/login" \
+        --data "$(jq -nc --arg u "$name" --arg p "$password" '{username:$u,password:$p}')")"
+    [[ "$status" == 200 ]] || { echo "Login failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; return 1; }
+}
+
+get_status() {
+    curl -sS -o "$response_file" -w '%{http_code}' -b "$1" "$BASE_URL$2"
+}
+
+delete_status() {
+    curl -sS -o "$response_file" -w '%{http_code}' -b "$1" -X DELETE "$BASE_URL$2"
+}
+
+login "$admin_jar" "$SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME" "$SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS"

+if [[ "$request_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then

+            }
+        login "$user_jar" "$user_name" "$SECMAN_USER_PASS"
+        status="$(delete_status "$user_jar" "/api/vulnerability-exception-requests/$request_id/delete")"
+        [[ "$status" == 204 ]] || { echo "Request cleanup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1; }
+    elif [[ "$status" != 404 ]]; then
+        echo "Request lookup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+
+if [[ "$asset_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    status="$(get_status "$admin_jar" "/api/assets/$asset_id")"
+    if [[ "$status" == 200 ]]; then
+        jq -e --argjson id "$asset_id" --arg name "$asset_name" \
+            '.id==$id and .name==$name' "$response_file" >/dev/null || {
+                echo "Asset identity mismatch; preserving it" >&2; exit 1;
+            }
+        status="$(delete_status "$admin_jar" "/api/assets/$asset_id")"
+        [[ "$status" == 204 || "$status" == 200 ]] || {
+            echo "Asset cleanup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1;
+        }
+    elif [[ "$status" != 404 ]]; then
+        echo "Asset lookup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+
+if [[ "$user_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    status="$(get_status "$admin_jar" "/api/users/$user_id")"
+    if [[ "$status" == 200 ]]; then
+        jq -e --argjson id "$user_id" --arg name "$user_name" --arg email "$user_email" \
+            '.id==$id and .username==$name and .email==$email' "$response_file" >/dev/null || {
+                echo "User identity mismatch; preserving it" >&2; exit 1;
+            }
+        status="$(delete_status "$admin_jar" "/api/users/$user_id")"
+        [[ "$status" == 204 || "$status" == 200 ]] || {
+            echo "User cleanup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1;
+        }
+    elif [[ "$status" != 404 ]]; then
+        echo "User lookup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+
+temp="$(mktemp "$MANIFEST.XXXXXX")"
+jq --arg cleaned "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '.cleanedAt=$cleaned' "$MANIFEST" > "$temp"
+mv "$temp" "$MANIFEST"
+echo "Manual fixture cleanup completed: $MANIFEST"

+
+get_status() {
+    curl -sS -o "$response_file" -w '%{http_code}' -b "$1" "$BASE_URL$2"
+}
+
+delete_status() {
+    curl -sS -o "$response_file" -w '%{http_code}' -b "$1" -X DELETE "$BASE_URL$2"
+}

+login "$admin_jar" "$SECMAN_ADMIN_NAME" "$SECMAN_ADMIN_PASS"

+            }

+        status="$(delete_status "$user_jar" "/api/vulnerability-exception-requests/$request_id/delete")"

+
+if [[ "$asset_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then

+    if [[ "$status" == 200 ]]; then
+        jq -e --argjson id "$asset_id" --arg name "$asset_name" \
+            '.id==$id and .name==$name' "$response_file" >/dev/null || {
+                echo "Asset identity mismatch; preserving it" >&2; exit 1;
+            }
+        status="$(delete_status "$admin_jar" "/api/assets/$asset_id")"
+        [[ "$status" == 204 || "$status" == 200 ]] || {
+            echo "Asset cleanup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1;
+        }
+    elif [[ "$status" != 404 ]]; then
+        echo "Asset lookup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+
+if [[ "$user_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    status="$(get_status "$admin_jar" "/api/users/$user_id")"
+    if [[ "$status" == 200 ]]; then
+        jq -e --argjson id "$user_id" --arg name "$user_name" --arg email "$user_email" \
+            '.id==$id and .username==$name and .email==$email' "$response_file" >/dev/null || {
+                echo "User identity mismatch; preserving it" >&2; exit 1;
+            }
+        status="$(delete_status "$admin_jar" "/api/users/$user_id")"
+        [[ "$status" == 204 || "$status" == 200 ]] || {
+            echo "User cleanup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1;
+        }
+    elif [[ "$status" != 404 ]]; then
+        echo "User lookup failed (HTTP $status)" >&2; exit 1
+    fi
+fi

+temp="$(mktemp "$MANIFEST.XXXXXX")"
+jq --arg cleaned "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '.cleanedAt=$cleaned' "$MANIFEST" > "$temp"
+mv "$temp" "$MANIFEST"
+echo "Manual fixture cleanup completed: $MANIFEST"

threatModel.summary: SecMan is a Micronaut/Kotlin security-management backend with Astro/React, CLI, MCP, scanner integrations, MariaDB, and a Go mobile relay. The reviewed changes add a bounded asset overview, multi-IP CrowdStrike ingestion, configurable isolated test startup, and runner-owned E2E database lifecycle.
assets: User identities, password hashes, JWTs, MFA state, API keys, and delegated identities
Asset, vulnerability, workgroup, risk, requirements, integration, and notification data
Production/test database separation and runner ownership
Mobile relay snapshot confidentiality and schema compatibility
trustBoundaries: Browser/external client to backend authentication: AuthController.kt:135-230
Authenticated caller to scoped assets: AssetFilterService.kt:18-161
Scanner account to integration ingestion: IntegrationController.kt:14-46
Browser and non-browser MCP callers: McpOriginValidationFilter.kt:29-100
Backend to relay/mobile client: RelayDtos.kt:16-19, RelaySnapshotBuilder.kt:90-119, src/relay/internal/api/api.go:74-89
Isolated E2E runner to MariaDB/local services: scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh:21-27,49-75,80-85,108-136
attackerCapabilities: Control ordinary authenticated inputs and data available to their assigned role
Submit scanner payloads through authorized integration/import accounts
Trigger browser-origin requests and repository test arguments
Cannot initially control ADMIN credentials, pass-cli secrets, database administrator access, trusted server configuration, or relay ingest credentials
securityObjectives: Enforce endpoint roles and AssetFilterService scoping
Bind all SQL values and constrain identifiers
Keep JWTs and secrets out of JavaScript, source, logs, and response DTOs
Delete only provably runner-owned E2E databases
Preserve credentialed CORS, security headers, relay schema, and audit invariants
assumptions: Static committed-range review only; runtime exposure and production configuration are unverified
Uncommitted frontend/E2E changes were reviewed separately
No reportable vulnerability was inferred from ordinary authorized behavior or local operator-controlled test configuration

coverage.inventoryStrategy: Workbench changed-source inventory; all 25 items reviewed sequentially

surfaces.riskArea: Shell injection, credential handling, production database destruction
surfaces.notes: Reviewed scripts/import.sh, scripts/manual/cleanup-test-data.sh, scripts/release-e2e-test.sh, scripts/runbackendtests.sh, scripts/startbackenddev.sh, and scripts/startfrontenddev.sh. Arguments are quoted or static; destructive database operations are limited to generated regex-constrained secman_e2e identifiers with matching ownership markers/manifests.

surfaces.riskArea: Default credentials and test-to-production boundary bypass
surfaces.notes: Reviewed src/backendng/build.gradle.kts, DefaultAdminBootstrapper.kt, application.yml. Isolated credentials are accepted only with an exact loopback secman_e2e JDBC target; production bootstrap retains random credentials.

surfaces.riskArea: Authorization bypass, SQL injection, unbounded reads, sensitive-field leakage
surfaces.notes: Reviewed AssetController.kt, AssetOverviewQueryService.kt, Asset.kt, CloudIdentifierDisplay.kt, and V278__asset_ip_addresses.sql. Non-global callers are restricted by AssetFilterService IDs before bound native-query filters and pagination; response fields remain scoped asset metadata.

surfaces.riskArea: Unbounded attacker data, SSRF, data-integrity loss
surfaces.notes: Reviewed CrowdStrikeVulnerabilityBatchDto.kt, CrowdStrikeVulnerabilityImportService.kt, VulnerabilityStorageService.kt, CrowdStrikeApiClientImpl.kt, and CrowdStrikeVulnerabilityDto.kt. Address sets are capped, trimmed, and sent to a fixed existing provider endpoint; no caller-selected destination or query construction was introduced.

surfaces.surface: Frontend asset overview and auth helpers
surfaces.riskArea: Client-side authorization, XSS/token exposure, proxy trust
surfaces.notes: Reviewed astro.config.mjs, AssetManagement.tsx and related tests/services, ProductsOverview tests, installedProductService.ts, and auth.ts. Backend remains the authorization boundary; HttpOnly-cookie auth is unchanged; URL filters are encoded with URLSearchParams; the E2E proxy override is environment-gated and loopback startup is enforced by the runner.
